title: Competitive Programming — High School Mastery
description: The problem-solving capstone of the Vietnamese HSG path: not more algorithms, but the working method — reading constraints, discovering the key observation, synthesizing techniques, proving correctness, optimizing, debugging plausible-but-wrong code, building counterexamples, stress testing, and harvesting partial scores — drilled through 14 process-first modules and graded in the C++20 sandbox.
audience: Students who finished the HSG Advanced and HSG Intensive courses (or equivalent) and can already implement advanced algorithms; the goal now is independent mastery of unfamiliar HSG and olympiad-style problems.
outcomes: Infer the algorithm class from constraints alone and state the operation budget before coding
Decompose an unfamiliar statement into a mathematical model and a subproblem plan
Discover invariants, parity, monotonicity, and exchange arguments by structured experimentation
Prove greedy and DP correctness, and construct counterexamples for plausible-but-wrong approaches
Synthesize combined techniques (DP + data structures, graphs + DP, offline + sweeps) under one budget
Optimize a working solution: find the bottleneck, apply the acceleration, prove the new bound
Debug compiled, sample-passing wrong code and repair it with minimal reasoning
Stress-test with a brute/reference/generator harness and maximize partial score under contest pressure
